messages:
sara: Heads up — hit drift during the gpufleet module canary (tf-mod v4.2.0) in us-west-2. GitOps applied automatically and we created 3 extra GPU nodes and a KMS alias with the old key id. :grimacing:

mike: Ugh. Did the reconciler show a plan or just apply?

sara: It auto-applied. The operator was on auto-apply mode for that repo (mistakenly). We should pause that repo. :eyes:

jordan: Can you paste the error from the apply or plan that failed for the KMS?

sara: Paste below — this was from the apply log right before the reconcile:
```
Error: Error creating google_kms_crypto_key
  on modules/kms/main.tf line 42, in resource "google_kms_crypto_key" "model_keys":
  42: resource "google_kms_crypto_key" "model_keys" {

  AlreadyExists: Resource already exists in a different project or with a different key_id
  detailed_message: "Key alias projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/rw-keyring/cryptoKeys/model-keys already points to key_id \"projects/oldproj/locations/global/keyRings/rw-keyring/cryptoKeys/model-keys\"
```

hemant: Sounds like a key alias rename collision. We moved the key between projects during the last security migration and the alias wasn't reconciled across regions.

mike: Also the extra GPUs — any quota errors?

sara: Yes, we hit a regional GPU quota when the autoscaler tried to allocate more; the operator retried and created the nodes in a different subnetwork to satisfy scheduling, which is why it looks like 3 spurious nodes. Plan output: 
```
+ google_compute_instance.gpu-node["gpufleet-3"]
+ google_compute_instance.gpu-node["gpufleet-4"]
+ google_compute_instance.gpu-node["gpufleet-5"]

Note: apply succeeded for instances but failed for kms resource.
```

jordan: We need to prevent mixed success states. Action items: 1) pause GitOps auto-apply for that repo, 2) pin tf-module to v4.1.x for the rest of fleet while we resolve 4.2.0, 3) perform a state audit for KMS alias ownership.

sara: Agreed. I've paused auto-apply on the repo and opened PR to pin the module in the overlay: 
```yaml
module_sources:
  - name: gpufleet
    source: registry.redwood/tf/gpufleet
    version: 4.1.7
```

hemant: For KMS, we should avoid re-creating alias. Proposed steps: 
- Create a temporary alias with suffix `-rollback` pointing to the old key_id
- Run `terraform state mv` if resource addresses diverged
- Then run a guarded apply to switch alias to canonical key once teams sign-off

mike: What exact state mv command do you expect?

hemant: Something like:
```
# move legacy resource to new module address if needed
terraform state mv "module.legacy_kms.google_kms_crypto_key.model_keys" "module.gpufleet.google_kms_crypto_key.model_keys"
```

jordan: Be careful — do this during a maintenance window and snapshot the state. Also update the lockfile/registry pin so other repos can't pick up v4.2.0 automatically.

sara: I've created an incident page and added timelines: short window (1h) at 09:30 UTC to run the state ops, then re-run apply in plan-only mode, then confirm no further auto-applies. Link: https://redwood.example/internal/incidents/1893456789

deploy-bot: gitops/repo-redwood/gpufleet overlay: auto-apply disabled by sara at 2026-03-18T09:10:02Z

mike: Also let's add a pre-apply check in our operator to detect KMS alias cross-project references and abort with a clear error. We shouldn't rely on apply-time errors.

hemant: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to the operator to run `gcloud kms crypto-keys get-iam-policy` (or equivalent) and compare key ids referenced by alias before apply. If mismatch -> block.

jordan: And add a canary rollout setting on the module registry so smaller fleets pick up v4.2.0 only when a flag is flipped. We need a lockfile approach for Terraform registry imports.

sara: For immediate mitigation I've: 
- paused auto-apply (done)
- pinned module in the overlay PR (open)
- scheduled the state mv window (09:30 UTC)
- notified oncall and security teams

mike: Thanks. After the state ops we should also run a full inventory: list all gpufleet instances across regions and mark any lab/stale nodes for drain. Script: 
```sh
# basic example
gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"name~gpufleet\" --format=\"table(name,zone,status)\"
```

sara: I'll own the inventory and drains. hemant please own the KMS state move. jordan you own the module pin PR and operator guard. I'll post a short postmortem after we close the incident.

jordan: ack. Will add follow-up tickets: operator guard + registry canary + pipeline pause docs.

mike: One more ask — add a cost estimate for the extra 3 GPUs (we should billback to the testing pool). I'll calculate and add to the incident.

sara: Will include cost in the postmortem.

deploy-bot: incident/1893456789 updated: status -> in_progress

sara: thanks all. I'll update once the state move completes. :thumbsup:
